scenes.title: The Same Kinds and Parts
scenes.summary: Epic has the kinds and parts of tragedy except song and spectacle, and Homer used them all: the Iliad simple and full of suffering, the Odyssey complex and full of character.

scenes.title: Length
scenes.summary: Epic may be longer, because narrative can present many parts happening at once, which gives grandeur and variety.

scenes.title: The Heroic Meter
scenes.summary: Experience has fitted the heroic meter to epic as the most stately and weighty; Chaeremon's mixing of meters is absurd.

scenes.title: Homer Speaks Little
scenes.summary: Homer alone knows how little the poet should speak in his own person: after a brief prelude he brings on a man or a woman, each with a character.

scenes.title: The Irrational and the Marvelous
scenes.summary: Epic admits the irrational, the source of wonder: the pursuit of Hector would be ridiculous on the stage. Homer taught the others to tell lies as they should, by false inference, as in the Bath.

scenes.title: Probable Impossibilities
scenes.summary: Prefer probable impossibilities to unconvincing possibilities; keep the irrational outside the plot, as Oedipus' ignorance of Laius' death, not as in the Electra or the Mysians. Homer sweetens the landing on Ithaca; brilliant diction belongs to the slack parts.
